prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one complete full-bleed portrait 2:3 tarot illustration, Page of Cups. The first 1 reference image(s) are exact Dragon Quest character identity/costume references; the LAST is ONLY the approved deck ink/color/texture style, not a scene or person to copy.
Scene and exact characters: Actual DQXI Sylvando, elegant male performer with slick black hair tied back, expressive eyes, gray-and-cream paneled performer tunic trimmed with small pom-poms, red sleeves, brown belt and purple boots. He stands on a quiet seaside shore with a playful sensitive smile, holding exactly ONE golden chalice. A single little blue fish peeks visibly from the water inside that cup, looking at him. No other cups, no sword or dagger, no text. Gentle waves and open sky, imaginative friendly energy. Keep his exact DQXI identity and outfit, not an original generic page.
Shared deck art direction: faithfully drawn Akira Toriyama Dragon Quest characters, clean confident black ink outlines, expressive recognizable faces, crisp hand-painted cel color blocks, restrained shadows and a subtle watercolor-paper grain matching the approved illustration. Original illustration, NOT a 3D screenshot, product photograph, plush, collage or card mockup. Full-bleed single cohesive artwork edge to edge, mobile-readable clear silhouettes and large key symbols.
Hard constraints: no title, no typography, no letters or numerals, no UI, no watermark/logo, no borders or card frame. Any writing, decorative labels, copyright line, duplicate background portraits or layout boxes on reference sheets must NOT appear. Preserve actual named DQ characters, hairstyle/clothing/colors, not generic original substitutes. Keep the stated number of tarot objects exact; avoid incidental extra cups/swords/coins/wands. Do not mix in characters from other franchises.
visual_review: Sylvando official black tied-back hair and gray-cream/red performer costume preserved. Exactly one chalice with one visible little fish, seaside scene, no text/frame; consistent deck art.
